correctness.rationale: PASS. Verified printed Hilbert-space Theorem 3.1 hypothesis ||a||_2² < A/||L|| conflicts with its own proof R=||L||²||a||_2² requiring R<A. For any A>0,t>1 on H=C and singleton measure, K=I, Lambda=√A I, L=tI, a=-√A/t: original A-tight, |a|²=A/t² < A/t, but Lambda+aLK*=0 and no lower K-frame bound. In particular independent exact test A=4,t=3,a=-2/3 cancels. The valid strict universal norm-only threshold ||a||_2² < A/||L||² yields lower bound (√A-||L||||a||_2)^2 via reverse triangle; boundary equality can cancel. Later Hilbert-C* module theorem repeats the mismatch; scalar Hilbert-C module already refutes it, with adjointable-analysis assumptions for the repaired general form.
